newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate drops to new post-crisis low.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate drops to new post-crisis low.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed down 70 basis points to 17.50 pesos on Tuesday, its lowest rate since the 1994 peso devaluation crisis.
Traders said rates fell on ample market liquidity, for which reason the central bank drained 5.442 billion pesos from the market.
"The market had been awash in liquidity since the open but the game turned around after the central bank participated. Dealing slowed down and the fall in rates was halted," a trader said.
Traders noted that Banco de Mexico assigned its secondary auctions at longer maturities and higher rates than usual, which led many to cut their earlier estimates for falls on primary rates.
A Reuters survey of eight money market traders in Mexico City showed they expected Banco de Mexico, the country's central bank, to assign bellwether 28-day Cetes at 18.86 percent.

This would be a fall of 60 basis points since last week's auction and a rate unseen since an abrupt devaluation of the Mexican peso triggered a financial crisis and severe economic recession in December 1994.
"By draining liquidity at ever greater maturities, the central bank is sending signals it wants the fall in primary rates to be reined in," another dealer said.
Dealers had been expected falls of greater than 100 basis points in early trade.
Overnight rates on bank paper also closed down, by 40 basis points to 19.80 percent.
Liquidity of 192 million pesos was scheduled to return to the system on Wednesday from prior central bank .
